To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The relative quantification of a target gene in comparison to a control gene in real time PCR is based on the real time PCR efficiency and the crossing point difference between the target and the control gene; (ii) The crossing point difference is calculated as crossing point of the target gene minus crossing point of the control gene; and (iii) The real time PCR efficiency is calculated as (E) = 10((1/slope) – 1)

a mathematical model was established that allows for accurate and reproducible quantification in real-time RT PCR without calibration curves and that the model is based on the PCR efficiencies and the relative crossing points of an unknown sample and the control.
